result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Sparkling has consent-free affiliate and transaction-successor assignment rights, Garman requires Sparkling’s consent subject to reasonableness and cannot assign to a Sparkling competitor, and Sparkling’s change of control creates no termination right. However, it goes beyond the stated position by permitting assignments “in whole or in part,” adding reorganizations and business-line transactions, and imposing notice on Sparkling. Section 20(d) is also repetitive, and the opening cross-reference in Section 3(c) could be drafted more precisely so it clearly modifies only the assignment prohibition rather than the separate transfer, lease, export, and sublicense restrictions.
